content:
If President Trump truly wants to see Kaitlan Collins laugh, he should have tuned in to CNN last night.

The president's favourite reporter was beside herself laughing during an appearance on The Source as she reported on the embarrassing scene in which Missouri Republican Senator Eric Schmitt inadvertently exposed himself while questioning former special counsel Jack Smith a day earlier. Collins also struggled to contain her laughter during the hearing at the response from Alabama Republican Senator Katie Britt, eventually summing up the entire disaster in one line.

"This is truly one of the most epic moments in Congressional hearing history," Collins said through her laughter.

During the hearing, Schmitt asked Smith: "Were you at the Warriors-Hawks NBA game on February 3, 2024?"

After Smith said he wasn't with a confused look on his face, Schmitt launched into an explanation for his line of questioning, noting that the game took place in Atlanta just a day after Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis admitted to having an affair with another prosecutor, Nathan Wade. Willis was, like Smith, in the midst of prosecuting Trump for his alleged efforts to interfere in the 2020 presidential election.

Schmitt also presented what he believed to be evidence in the form of a screenshot of a conversation with a member of Smith's staff, claiming Smith had attended a "Hawks" game that day.

But what Schmitt clearly thought would be a slam dunk turned out to be an own goal. After some back-and-forth, Smith finally remembered that he had indeed attended a Hawks game that day, but not the Atlanta Hawks and not an NBA game.

He had gone to an Iowa Hawkeyes vs. Maryland Terrapins women's college basketball game in Maryland to watch then-up-and-coming star Caitlin Clark, now in the WNBA.

Progressive media outlet MeidasTouch located and shared footage of Smith at the Iowa-Maryland game on Feb. 3, 2024, and HuffPost also confirmed via a spokesperson for Smith that the man in the footage was indeed him.

After playing several clips of Schmitt's confusion over the difference between the Atlanta Hawks and the Iowa Hawkeyes on her CNN show—barely containing her own laughter—Collins turned to one of her guests, Democratic strategist Paul Begala, for his take on the circus.

"Oh, poor Senator Schmitt," Begala said with dripping sarcasm. "I'm glad they did this, OK? Because now we know what a brilliant guy Senator Schmitt is."

Begala continued: "This is so stupid. I have to say it. And the fact that we even did this hearing is so stupid. We are 35 days out from an election, gas is $4.50 a gallon, diesel is $6.50 a gallon, ground beef is $6.92 a pound... If people were sour on the Republicans before the hearing and wanted a change, they're going to be even more sour after this hearing."

Collins' other guest, Republican strategist Shermichael Singleton, agreed with Begala, emphatically insisting that the GOP must focus on affordability issues ahead of the November midterms.

When Collins asked Singleton if he thought Republicans should have invited Smith to testify before Congress, Singleton responded with exasperation: "For what?! What did this accomplish?!"
